definitions.active: A well currently in operation. The chart reports marginal wells as a separate category.
definitions.marginal: An active well with average production below 10 barrels of oil equivalent per day.
definitions.operating: Active plus marginal well licences. Marginal wells are active wells in AER’s definition.
definitions.inactive: A well that has not produced oil or gas, injected fluids, or disposed of waste for 6 or 12 months, depending on type and risk.
definitions.new: A drilled well that has not produced.
definitions.decommissioned: A well permanently sealed and taken out of service; also called abandoned.
definitions.reclamationCertified: A well whose site has received a reclamation certificate after return to equivalent land capacity.
definitions.reclamationExempt: A well decommissioned before reclamation requirements came into effect (1963 in some areas, otherwise 1978).

source.title: Well Status — number of licensed wells in each stage of the life cycle

limitations: Counts cover well licences, including orphaned wells. They are not counts of mapped records or individual production strings.
AER defines marginal wells as active wells. Operating is the sum of the separately displayed Active and Marginal categories.
Past years are December 31 snapshots. The current-year CSV supplies only the year; its month is unknown. Retrieval date is not observation date.
These provincial totals cannot be filtered by a map area, operator, text search or mapped-record status.
